events.title: ¡Puro Ritmo! The Musical Journey of Salsa
events.venue: Molina Family Latino Gallery at the National Museum of American History
events.description: From the streets of Havana to the dancefloors of New York and beyond, "¡Puro Ritmo!" explores how Afro-Cuban music evolved into a defining sound in the U.S. This bilingual exhibition traces salsa’s roots and rise through nearly 300 objects. Highlighting artists from Tito Puente and Celia Cruz to local legends and hidden pioneers, "¡Puro Ritmo!" celebrates salsa as one of America’s great musical traditions. A centerpiece of the exhibition is the presentation of five ensembles and five pairs of shoes worn by Celia Cruz, celebrated worldwide as the Queen of Salsa. Gifted by the Estate of Celia Cruz, the five dresses and a pair of shoes are now part of the Latino Museum’s permanent collection. The outfits will rotate throughout the exhibition’s two-and-a-half-year run, offering visitors multiple opportunities to experience Cruz’s vibrant stage presence.In addition to Cruz, the exhibition highlights iconic figures such as Tito Puente and Eddie Palmieri, as well as influential artists including Arsenio Rodríguez, Graciela, Ray Barretto and Willie Colón. It also explores the industry-shaping impact of Fania Records and its cofounders, Jerry Masucci and Johnny Pacheco.

events.title: “In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness”
events.description: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History will lead the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. “In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness,” will open May 14, featuring 250 objects, across 250,000 square feet of the museum’s three public floors, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy Revolutionary War artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia. This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. A favorite with visitors is the Star-Spangled Banner the 1813 flag that inspired the National Anthem. A free guide will be available to help locate the artifacts, which range from the 1700s to the 21st century. The museum will also offer an extensive website to online visitors and those who want to take a deeper dive into this history following their visit. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events will welcome all Americans to reflect and commemorate on this significant anniversary. It closes in December 2026.

events.title: Are You Now or Have You Ever Been?
events.venue: Arena Stage at the Mead Center for American Theater
events.description: Straight from Off-Broadway comes Eric Bentley's timely American docudrama, Are You Now or Have You Ever Been?, directed by Tony Award winner Anna D. Shapiro. This electrifying story drops you into the tense world of the 1940s House Un-American Activities Committee hearings, where fame offered no protection and political pressure could end a career. Using the original transcripts, the play features the words of artists like Arthur Miller, Jerome Robbins, Paul Robeson, Elia Kazan, Lillian Hellman, Abe Burrows, and Lionel Stander as they faced impossible choices: defend their integrity, protect their careers, or betray their peers. And yet the probing, chilling questions posed by the committee are as powerful as the testimonies themselves, revealing a climate of intimidation and moral conflict that resonates far beyond its time.

Through approximately 90 paintings, drawings, and watercolors from the 1920s to the mid-1960s, this exhibition reflects in depth for the first time on the artistic exchange between these three artists, the experiences they shared, and the support they gave one another. Many works have never been on public view. IMAGE: Milton Avery, Black Sea, 1959, The Phillips Collection, Acquired 1965; © 2025 Milton Avery Trust/Artists Rights Society (ARS), New York

events.title: Embassy Row Walking Tour
events.description: Learn about the people and places that have turned this district into one of the most exclusive neighborhoods in the city and the center of the foreign diplomatic community. Massachusetts Avenue is home to a dazzling array of international diplomatic missions, each embassy offering a glimpse into their country’s culture and heritage. These buildings not only host diplomatic affairs but also offer events that celebrate their respective nations’ rich histories and traditions. A historic private club dating back to 1878, the Cosmos Club is housed in a majestic mansion that exudes sophistication. Anderson House, a marvel of early 20th-century design, was once the winter residence of Larz and Isabel Anderson. Today, it serves as the headquarters of the Society of the Cincinnati. Nestled in the Kalorama neighborhood, the Woodrow Wilson House is a lovingly preserved time capsule of the former president’s life. This historic site features period furnishings, personal artifacts, and educational displays about Wilson’s presidency and legacy. A hidden gem in the city, the Spanish Steps provides a quiet and picturesque escape from the urban bustle. events.description: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History will lead the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness will span three floors and 300,000 square feet, featuring 250 significant objects, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia . This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a year-long series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events begin in the spring of 2026, welcoming all Americans to reflect on the enduring and sometimes delayed or denied promises that surround the ongoing pursuit of life, liberty and happiness.

events.title: Miguel Braceli: UNBURIAL (exhibition)
events.address: St. John's College, 60 College Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21401
events.description: Unburial treats absence as a site for learning and reflection. The void left by the Liberty Tree becomes more than metaphor: an art intervention transforms it into a place to be repurposed and reclaimed through rituals and celebrations that probe what freedom means today. On the front lawn, where the Liberty Tree once stood, the artist Miguel Braceli has installed a 40'-diameter circle of cemetery vases filled with common wildflowers. It calls attention to the tree's absence and reclaims it as a tree for all people, not just the privileged and elite (e.g., the Sons of Liberty and the four Annapolis signers of the Declaration of Independence). In the museum, Braceli, with the help of a team of fabricators, created three enormous murals and two other works. The murals perform an autopsy of the tree. The largest multiplies the tulip poplar's distinctive leaf shape across a 33'-long wall in a wind-swept swirl of energy (the leaves were made from stencils of the Liberty Tree scion's actual leaves). A second mural abstracts the tree's tangled root system into a water-bearing drawing (using PVC tubing) that sprouts purple carnations. The third mural's subject is the tree's massive trunk, which was cut to pieces in 1999, with much of the wood later finding commemorative as Liberty Tree guitars, conference tables, and bible boxes. Onto nine chalkboards, Braceli has mounted nine pieces of raw wood, each supporting live orchids. What can we learn anew from this tree?, it seems to ask. The two other works urge us to turn away from nation-state identities and to look and listen more closely to nature. A sculptural ear is mounted onto the red silhouette of a rose petal, borrowed from the work of Columbia-born, Venezuela-based artist Roberto Obregoń. Nearby, a flag of yellow roses hangs from a flagpole that has been fabricated from a branch. Admission & Hours Free & open to the public Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Open Friday, 12 to 7:30 p.m. Parking

events.title: National Archives & American History Museum Tour
events.description: The Declaration of Independence. The Star-Spangled Banner. Julia Child’s kitchen. The original US Constitution. Two of the most important buildings on the National Mall — and most visitors only scratch the surface of what’s inside them. This three-hour tour takes you inside the Smithsonian American History Museum and the National Archives with a professional guide who knows exactly what to show you, what to skip, and what the plaques don’t tell you.

events.title: National Mall Walking Tour & Washington Monument
events.description: Let a fun and energetic tour guide explain the history, symbolism, and stories behind the memorials on the National Mall! You'll hear stories of real people the memorials honor, understand why they are important, and what exciting features they hide. On this tour, we will explore: Lincoln Memorial - see the famous statue, hear about our 16th President, see where MLK, Jr. stood to give the "I Have A Dream Speech." Reflecting Pool - where Forrest Gump ran through to see Jenny. Vietnam Veterans Memorial - hear the stories behind the wall of names of those killed and missing in action. WWII Memorial - find Kilroy hidden amongst the columns honoring the states and territories. White House - see the south lawn of the White House where Marine One lands. We include tickets to the top of the Washington Monument for guests on our tour.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: NextStop Theatre’s:  The Elaborate Entrance of Chad Deity
events.description: NextStop Theatre presents The Elaborate Entrance of Chad Deity from November 5th–29th, 2026, at 269 Sunset Park Drive in Herndon, Fairfax County, Virginia. This Pulitzer Prize-finalist comedy by Kristoffer Diaz body-slams the world of pro-wrestling, pop culture, and the performance of identity. Told through the eyes of Macedonio "The Mace" Guerra, a gifted wrestler stuck being paid to lose to a bigger-named star in the ring, this knockout satire takes on cultural stereotypes, media spectacle, and the courage it takes to say no. A bold, tour-de-force comedy that leaves it all on the mat! Directed by Stefan Sittig, a multi-disciplined theatre veteran with 140+ productions across New York City, international venues, and D.C.-area theaters, the production features Sittig's expertise as a Helen Hayes Award-nominated director, choreographer, and fight director. Kristoffer Diaz, the playwright and screenwriter, is also known for his musical Hell's Kitchen (created with Alicia Keys), nominated for 13 Tony Awards and currently running on Broadway. Audience advisories include strong language, simulated violence/fighting, racial stereotypes, and flashing lights and haze effects. The 2nd Sunday matinee will be a mask-required performance (masks provided). The Elaborate Entrance of Chad Deity combines theatrical excellence, sharp satire, and bold storytelling in Fairfax County, Virginia. Tickets are available through Ovationtix at https://ci.ovationtix.com/34310 . Box office: boxoffice@nextstoptheatre.org / (703) 481-5930x1. events.title: Past and Future Cities
events.description: A new exhibition traces the nation's history through the development of its built urban environments. A new exhibition offers a fascinating exploration of the nation's history by tracing the intricate development of its built urban environments. Through a carefully curated selection of artifacts, photographs, and interactive displays, the exhibition highlights how cities and towns have evolved over the years, reflecting the socio-economic, cultural, and political shifts that have shaped them. From the architectural styles of bygone eras to modern urban planning initiatives, visitors can gain insight into how the physical landscapes of these urban areas tell the story of the people who inhabit them. This journey through time allows attendees to appreciate not only the artistic and historical significance of these structures but also the stories behind them, illuminating the complex relationship between society and the built environment throughout the nation’s history.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
events.address: 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005
events.description: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027 This landmark exhibition of over 80 quilted objects that traces how Black women leaving the Jim Crow South stitched a legacy of survival, connection, and resilience across generations. Routed West features work by more than 70 artists spanning 120 years. The show tells a uniquely American story through quilts from the Second Great Migration, a mass movement of five million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West, to today. Many of those who migrated in search of a more equitable life carried quilts—for warmth and protection, as well as emblems of ancestral memory and cultural survival. Routed West traces the flow and flourishing of quilts in the context of the Second Great Migration, a mass movement of approximately five million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West between 1940 and 1970 in search of a more equitable life. Many of the hundreds of thousands of migrants who arrived in California carried quilts for warmth and protection, as containers for ancestral memory, and as emblems of cultural survival. Organized across several themes through more than 80 artworks with kaleidoscopic patterns, colors, and forms, Routed West offers a history of art through quilts’ joyful power in Black life. The quilts in the exhibition highlight artistic approaches such as repurposing work clothes, improvisational piecing, pattern-based quilting, and tying, practiced by those who would carry these works out of the South. Quilts by migrants from Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, and Texas, regions heavily represented in the westward movement of African Americans, reflect the ways in which these works become cherished heirlooms. events.title: Shifting Boundaries: Perspectives on American Landscapes
events.address: Jefferson Drive at 12th St., SW, Washington, DC
events.description: American painters Willard Metcalf, Dwight Tryon, Winslow Homer, and Abbott Thayer created profoundly beautiful views of the New England landscapes where they lived and worked. These paintings largely depict that environment as timeless and static. Shifting Boundaries looks at these works from a new angle by engaging a multiplicity of voices and viewpoints to explore what these paintings can tell us about changes to this region both past and present. As Shifting Boundaries reveals, the views these artists created of pasturelands in Massachusetts and of seascapes in Maine were transforming even as these artists recorded them. This reshaping of landscapes has only accelerated in the century since Metcalf, Tryon, Homer, and Thayer depicted them. Shifting Boundaries pilots a new mode of collaborative curatorial practice. NMAA Lunder Curator of American Art Diana Greenwold , curatorial assistant Mary Mulcahy , and interpretation specialists Liz Gardner and Amy Freesun partnered with Lauren Brandes (Smithsonian Gardens), Dennis Chestnut (Groundwork Anacostia River DC), Jerome Foster II (Waic Up), Elizabeth James-Perry (Aquinnah Wampanoag artist), Lorette Picciano (Rural Coalition), Stephanie Toothman (National Park Service), and Melinda Whicher (Smithsonian Gardens) to develop the themes for this exhibition, select works of art, and write object labels. The group’s perspectives, drawn from their individual areas of professional expertise and their own personal experiences, allow us to see new details in these stunning works of art. The landscapes become invitations to explore a century of human impact on New England land and water, the erasure of indigenous histories, and the environmental changes that are altering this region today.

events.title: The American Story
events.description: The National Archives Museum debuts a once-in-a generation redesign of its permanent exhibits: The American Story and the Discovery Center - connecting visitors with the National Archives in revolutionary ways. The American Story will showcase items and records in the National Archives that tell important moments in our nation's history. Visitors will get up close to more than 40 original artifacts and documents, including a rare 1823 Stone Engraving of the Declaration of Independence, George Washington's annotated copy of the Constitution, and presidential gifts including horseshoes to President Bush from Queen Elizabeth II. The American Story will be the first and only museum in Washington, DC to use artificial intelligence (AI) to bring each visitor a special, individualized opportunity to explore the records of the American people and engage with American history. This exhibit brings more than two million historic records to life, offering a personalized journey through our nation's past. This new museum experience provides all Americans with a special opportunity to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

events.title: The American Story
events.description: The National Archives Museum has opened its new flagship exhibition, The American Story, after a multi-year reimagination of its museum galleries, just in time to celebrate America’s Semiquincentennial. Innovative, engaging, and powered by artificial intelligence, The American Story brings more than two million historic records to life and offers visitors opportunities to personally connect their lives to our nation’s storied past. The American Story immerses guests in an interactive exploration of the people, ideas, and events that shaped 250 years of U.S. history through nine captivating galleries that spotlight categories of records in the National Archives. After selecting the topics of interest through AI- driven portals, visitors will be presented with historical content tailored to their individual interests that they can later revisit online. This exhibit features several dozen historic, original artifacts, documents, patents, and film slips, including: George Washington’s annotated draft Constitution The Louisiana Purchase Treaty Notable patents, including Thomas Edison’s lightbulb, Barbie, and Yoda from Star Wars Declassified records from the Cuban Missile Crisis and UFO sightings The first government sponsored film capturing the Wright Brothers’ test flight State gifts to Presidents, including horseshoes gifted by Queen Elizabeth II to President George H.W. Bush Immediately adjacent to the museum galleries is a reimagined Discovery Center, featuring educational arcade games and a classroom with hands-on civics education activities for children and families.

events.title: The Original Historic Georgetown Walking Tour
events.description: Georgetown’s shady lanes and cobblestone streets reflect another side of the Capital city. It is Washington’s historic neighborhood, where Presidents lived when they were Congressmen, where the Founding Fathers laid out the plans for the city on a tavern bar top, where women broke barriers, and where Black neighbors developed a tight-knit community despite prejudice. This tour covers history, architecture, and the stories of Georgetown's over 200 years of residents. You will see and hear stories of: Chesapeake & Ohio Canal - a waterway through the industrial part of the neighborhood. Old Stone House - oldest residential building in the district, now a National Park site. Homes of Jackie & John F. Kennedy - hear about their time in Georgetown before and after his assassination 18th and 19th Century Homes - learn about the diverse, historic architecture of the houses and the stories of those who have lived here. Look for original firemarks, coal chutes, ironworks, and gas lanterns. Hear stories of the Black Georgetown community, immigrants who shaped the neighborhood, and women who bucked social norms. Georgetown University - see the famous campus and learn how the neighborhood influenced it.

To Hear Her Speak: Black Women and Shakespeare
events.address: 201 E Capitol St. SE, Washington, DC 20003
events.description: For centuries, Black women have claimed Shakespeare, reshaping his words to assert their humanity, creativity, and power. To Hear Her Speak brings these voices into focus for the first time. Curated by Dr. Patricia Akhimie, Director of the Folger Institute, this landmark exhibition explores the histories of Black women in Shakespearean performance and highlights the ways in which Black women have engaged Shakespeare’s language, stories, and characters in their work. To Hear Her Speak also builds on new research about the presence of Black women in early modern Europe, and shows how they were represented (and misrepresented) by artists and writers of the day, including Shakespeare, whose Sonnet 130 inspired the exhibition’s title. Nearly 100 objects ranging from photographs, playbills, posters, books, diaries, illustrations, and costumes draw from the Folger collection as well as key loans. Together, they document the stories of Maya Angelou, Toni Morrison, Lorraine Hansberry, Mae Turner, Esther Rolle, Phillis Wheatley, and many others. To Hear Her Speak invites visitors to listen closely to the Black women who have used Shakespeare to shape careers, challenge exclusion, and insist upon their place in history. As actors, scholars, authors, artists, musicians, directors, and so much more—Black women have spoken Shakespeare’s words into new possibilities.

events.title: We Make History
events.description: As the nation commemorates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, "We Make History" explores how history happens, is preserved and shared. In Washington, D.C. and places around the country, many people were quietly keeping the records, building the collections, and developing the skills that would create America’s historical narrative. These community-based stories serve as the building blocks for 250 years of American history. Using the country’s anniversary as a milestone, the museum uses its community driven practice to celebrate local civic engagement and encourage local history keeping. This exhibition is a tribute to celebrating our communities and making possible a better understanding of our shared past. These stories are important to marking the Semiquincentennial because they help show the legacy of how people make history one act, one document, one story at a time. By bringing these stories to the forefront in 2026, the exhibit inspires the next generation to keep and share their own stories and records to add to America’s historical narrative. We Make History has an anticipated opening date of May 30, 2026.

events.title: Interwoven: A Tradition of Textiles
events.description: Textiles have long served as both functional objects and extraordinary works of art, woven into the fabric of everyday life and elevated by generations of makers. Hillwood's upcoming exhibition will be the first to focus on this essential yet unexplored aspect of the collection, showcasing the remarkable artistry, technical mastery, and cultural importance of textiles across centuries. Drawing from Hillwood's rich holdings, the exhibition invites visitors to consider the enduring power of textiles, not only as decorative or domestic objects but also as expressions of identity, devotion, innovation, and exquisite craftsmanship. Marjorie Merriweather Post's Collection Marjorie Merriweather Post maintained a reverence for textiles throughout her life, preserving antique lace samples, apparel from her girlhood, and examples of textile work created by the women in her family, including her mother, Ella Letitia Merriweather (1853-1912); her paternal aunt, Mary "Mollie" Stanley Post (1860-1925); and her grandmother, Caroline Lathrop Post (1824-1915). Post applied the same criteria to textiles as she did all her collecting: exquisite artisanship and intricate details. She collected handmade lace pieces and resplendent liturgical vestments and textiles from the Russian Orthodox Church, furnished her homes and personal spaces with sumptuous fabrics, and attired herself and her three daughters in the finest of fashions. Post also maintained a progressive approach to repurposing textiles, such as snipping embroidered sections of a daytime ensemble for an alternate use and upholstering chairs with an antique quilt. Textiles on View Organized into four sections, the exhibition will explore centuries' worth of historical textiles; the act of creating such fiber-based pieces; form and function, including lace, embroidery and needlepoint, and quilts and coverings; and commemorative textiles, which serve as relics of the past. events.title: Out of Bounds at The Kreeger Museum
events.description: Hamiltonian Artists and The Kreeger Museum are pleased to present Out of Bounds, an exhibition of the work of seven Hamiltonian Artists Alumni (Selin Balci, Larry W. Cook, Joyce Yu-Jean Lee, Christie Neptune, Allison Spence, Kyle Tata, and Jing (Ellen) Xu) on view at The Kreeger Museum from October 15 through December 31, 2026. Borrowed from the language of sport, Out of Bounds refers to the space beyond the limits of play. Figuratively, it can describe actions, ideas, or behaviors that go against accepted rules or expectations. Working across painting, photo, sculpture, video, and installation, the artists presented in Out of Bounds consider what it means to question, cross, or redraw established boundaries. The Hamiltonian alumni’s work will be exhibited alongside selected contemporary works from The Kreeger Museum's permanent collection, including artists Sam Gilliam, Frank Stella, Simmie Knox, and William Christenberry. Each of these artists was an iconoclast in their day, rejecting rigid geometries and traditional methods of paint application, and pushing the limits of fine art mediums and subject matter. The Hamiltonian alumni bring a similar spirit of ingenuity to their anti-disciplinary practices—experimenting with materials and challenging conventions of figuration and representation. Some may argue that boundaries exist to be dismantled; as so often, they are imposed to include and to exclude. This exhibition invites the viewer to reconsider who gets to define the rules, and who has the power to enforce them. What is at stake when boundaries are crossed? What becomes possible on the other side of spontaneity and risk? Each artist featured in Out of Bounds approaches these questions through acts of disruption and reimagining, pointing toward the vast possibilities that emerge when established structures are tested. events.title: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California
events.venue: National Museum of Women in the Arts
events.address: 1250 New York Ave. NW, Washington, DC 20005
events.description: Routed West: Twentieth-Century African American Quilts in California September 18, 2026 to January 17, 2027 This landmark exhibition of over 80 quilted objects that traces how Black women leaving the Jim Crow South stitched a legacy of survival, connection, and resilience across generations. Routed West features work by more than 70 artists spanning 120 years. The show tells a uniquely American story through quilts from the Second Great Migration, a mass movement of five million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West, to today. Many of those who migrated in search of a more equitable life carried quilts—for warmth and protection, as well as emblems of ancestral memory and cultural survival. Routed West traces the flow and flourishing of quilts in the context of the Second Great Migration, a mass movement of approximately five million African Americans from the rural South to cities in the North and West between 1940 and 1970 in search of a more equitable life. Many of the hundreds of thousands of migrants who arrived in California carried quilts for warmth and protection, as containers for ancestral memory, and as emblems of cultural survival. Organized across several themes through more than 80 artworks with kaleidoscopic patterns, colors, and forms, Routed West offers a history of art through quilts’ joyful power in Black life. The quilts in the exhibition highlight artistic approaches such as repurposing work clothes, improvisational piecing, pattern-based quilting, and tying, practiced by those who would carry these works out of the South. Quilts by migrants from Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Oklahoma, and Texas, regions heavily represented in the westward movement of African Americans, reflect the ways in which these works become cherished heirlooms. Dragonforce with Ensiferum and Rhapsody Of Fire
events.description: DragonForce is a British power metal band renowned for its blistering speed, virtuosic guitar work and larger-than-life approach to melodic metal. Their music combines soaring vocals, lightning-fast solos, symphonic elements and fantasy-inspired themes to create an exhilarating and highly energetic sound. Known for pushing the technical limits of the genre, the band has earned international acclaim for both its musicianship and its spectacular live performances. DragonForce remains one of the most recognizable and influential acts in modern power metal, celebrated for turning epic storytelling into high-octane musical adventures. Ensiferum is a Finnish folk metal band known for blending traditional folk melodies with powerful metal instrumentation and heroic themes. Their music often draws inspiration from mythology, history, nature and adventure, creating sweeping compositions that combine aggression with rich cultural influences. Featuring dynamic songwriting and a balance of melodic and heavy elements, the band has become a cornerstone of the folk metal genre. Ensiferum's energetic performances and immersive storytelling have earned them a dedicated international following. Rhapsody of Fire is an Italian symphonic power metal band celebrated for pioneering the fusion of classical orchestration, cinematic storytelling and metal. Their music is characterized by grand arrangements, epic narratives, virtuosic musicianship and fantasy-inspired concepts that transport listeners into imaginative worlds. Combining powerful vocals, orchestral textures and intricate compositions, the band helped define the sound of symphonic power metal for generations of artists and fans. Widely respected for their creativity and ambition, Rhapsody of Fire continues to stand as one of the genre's most influential and iconic acts.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Mental Reset: Sound Bath + Reiki : Thursday Evenings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Thursday is a weird day. The week isn't over, but you are. Mental Reset is one hour at the end of the workday where nobody needs anything from you. You come in, you lie down on a mat, you get a blanket and a bolster, and for the next sixty minutes your only job is to listen. I play crystal singing bowls, guide you through a short meditation so your mind has something to do besides replay the day, and offer Reiki while you rest. Most people tell me some version of the same thing afterward: the noise in their head finally turned down. Not off: down. Enough that they can go home and actually be home, instead of answering emails in their head at the dinner table. You don't need experience. You don't need to know how to meditate, and you definitely don't need to “clear your mind.” If you could do that, you wouldn't need this class. First-timers are in the room most weeks. There are ten spots. That's deliberate. It's a small room, I can see everyone in it, and it never feels like an event. It feels like an exhale. A few regulars started as skeptics; more than one of our Google reviews comes from someone who arrived doubting the whole thing and left surprised at how settled they felt. You don't have to believe in anything for an hour of sound and rest to do you some good. Run by Victoria Vita: CPA for 20+ years, healer for 7+. I sat behind a desk with a brain that wouldn't switch off for a long time before I found this work. Thursday nights are built for the person I used to be. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Come straight from work. Leave like the week let go of you first. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket, and bolster everything is here; you bring nothing • Small group: 10 people maximum, same teacher every week • Time at the end to sit up slowly, have water, and not rush out Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: U Streets Jazzed Up Cocktail Tour
events.description: Don’t know why its called Black Broadway? Don’t worry. We’ll explain it along the way, and you’ll be glad we did! After all, this is a history infused cocktail tour. And we believe the best way to connect to a city is through its flavors! Immerse yourself in the rhythmic heartbeat of U Street with our “Cocktail Couture & Jazz Beats” tour, where every note and sip is a celebration of culture, history, and refinement. Experience the perfect fusion of Black Broadway’s jazz heritage, Michelin Star cuisine, and expertly crafted cocktails. It’s the perfect night out for cocktail connoisseurs and jazz aficionados alike. Drink in the local spirit. We’ll visit several of our favorite bars and restaurants, carefully curated for their contributions to our story about the history of the neighborhood….and a couple have been awarded the famed Michelin star! Between the opportunities we’ve coordinated to imbibe and snack, you’ll see and hear all about the street art, architecture, and evolving history of this iconic DC neighborhood. We’ve preselected tasty snacks we think everyone will enjoy (and always have a vegetarian option – select the vegetarian option when you book) and you’ll have a choice between a couple of specialty cocktails at each stop. Our experience ends in a place where we think you might just choose to relax for a bit, so consider keeping the evening open after your tour! Aside from carefully curated cocktails, tastings and fascinating history, your experience includes custom photos of your tour. A portion of each tour ticket is donated to our charity partner and is enough to feed a local resident in need for the whole day, three full meals. *NOTE: Since this tour includes alcohol, we strongly suggest arriving and departing using public transportation, cabs, or ride share.

events.title: Whodunit Book Club at Kramers
events.description: About the Book Two women haunted by their sisters' unsolved disappearances band together in this captivating mystery from the #1 New York Times bestselling author of All Good People Here and host of the #1 true crime podcast Crime Junkie. Nicole “Nic” Monroe is in a rut. At twenty-four, she lives alone in a dinky apartment in her hometown of Mishawaka, Indiana, she’s just gotten a DWI, and she works the same dead-end job she’s been working since high school, a job she only has because her boss is a family friend and feels sorry for her. Everyone has felt sorry for her for the last seven years—since the day her older sister, Kasey, vanished without a trace. On the night Kasey went missing, her car was found over a hundred miles from home. The driver’s door was open and her purse was untouched in the seat next to it. The only real clue in her disappearance was Jules Connor, another young woman from the same area who disappeared in the same way, two weeks earlier. But with so little for the police to go on, both their cases eventually went cold. Nic wants nothing more than to move on—from her sister’s disappearance and the state it’s left her in. But then one day, Jules’s sister, Jenna Connor, walks into her life and offers Nic something she hasn’t felt in a long hope. What follows is a gripping tale of two sisters who will do anything to find their missing halves, even if it means destroying everything they’ve ever known. About the Club We'll be reading and discussing edge-of-your-seat thrillers each month! Feel free to grab a drink at the bar to enjoy during our book club discussion. Wander through the woods, soak in the crisp mountain air, and then cozy up in the Taproom with one of our warm seasonal drinks and hearty food specials from the kitchen. Guests are welcome to enjoy a stroll through the forest where you can find whimsy, merriment and endless amounts of holiday cheer at this holiday light display! Immerse yourself in a winter wonderland, and enjoy nostalgic scenes as you wander through the Blue Ridge Mountains. Learn more and get your tickets to The Christmas Trail at Dirt Farm here: https://dirtfarmbrewing.com/event/the-christmas-trail-at-dirt-farm-brewing/2026-11-27/ Whether you’re coming out from Washington D.C., Alexandria, Arlington, or Baltimore, or you’re just cruising over from Round Hill, Purcellville, Clarke County, or Winchester, we’re always glad to welcome friendly faces here in Bluemont—near or far. events.title: Crazy Chester - A Very Carrboro Tribute To The Band & The Last Waltz 50th Anniversary Tour w/ JP Hudson
events.description: Crazy Chester Formed in early 2020 for a series of one-off events in the piedmont region of North Carolina, Crazy Chester is a homegrown tribute act to The Band, consisting of Carrboro musicians Jones Bell (Mellow Swells, Ravary), Charles Cleaver (Big Star's Third, Fancy Gap, Lemon Sparks), Rob DiMauro (Heat Preacher, Mixtape Grab Bag, One After 919), Justin Ellis (Slow Teeth, Ravary, Easter Island, One After 919), and Rafael Green (solo artist, Ravary, One After 919), respectively recreating and playing the parts of Richard Manuel, Garth Hudson, Levon Helm, Rick Danko, and Robbie Robertson. For the sixth year in a row, Crazy Chester will be performing most of The Band's legendary farewell performance from Thanksgiving Day 1976, immortalized in the 1978 Martin Scorsese film "The Last Waltz" - complete with additional musicians and special local guests to play the songs originally performed in the film by Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, Neil Young, and many more. But this time - they're taking the show on the road to celebrate 50 Years of The Last Waltz. A show that must be seen to be believed. Full list of guest performers TBD!

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

Los Tigres del Norte
events.address: CFG Bank Arena 201 West Baltimore Street, Baltimore, MD 21201
events.description: Los Tigres del Norte are a pioneering norteño band whose accordion-led songs turn the rhythms of regional Mexican music into vivid stories of love, migration and life along the U.S.-Mexico border. Formed in Sinaloa in the late 1960s, the group built a decades-spanning catalog that includes the dramatic corrido “Contrabando y Traición,” the singalong favorite “La Puerta Negra” and “Jefe de Jefes.” Their honors include seven Grammy Awards and eight Latin Grammy Awards. The appeal lies in the storytelling as much as the sound: familiar melodies carry characters, heartbreak and lived experience from verse to verse.

events.description: Los Tucanes de Tijuana are a norteño group led by singer, songwriter and producer Mario Quintero Lara, celebrated for pairing narrative corridos with cumbias, romantic songs and party-ready rhythms. Since emerging from Tijuana in the late 1980s, they have built a wide-ranging catalog that includes the dance-floor favorite “La Chona,” “El Tucanazo” and the Grammy-nominated albums Jugo a la Vida, Imperio and 365 Días. Their music moves easily between storytelling and celebration, giving listeners both the vivid characters of a corrido and the irresistible pulse of a communal sing-along.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

A bold, tour-de-force comedy that leaves it all on the mat! Audience Advisories: strong language, simulated violence/fighting, racial stereotypes, flashing lights and haze effects. events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. His music is characterized by moody production, introspective lyricism, and emotionally honest storytelling that explores themes of love, heartbreak, personal growth, mental health and self-discovery. With a smooth vocal style and a deeply personal approach to songwriting, he has earned widespread acclaim for creating music that feels both vulnerable and relatable. 6LACK has established himself as one of the most influential voices in contemporary R&B through his unique artistry and genre-defying sound. Eem Triplin is an American rapper, singer, producer and songwriter recognized for his creative approach to modern hip-hop and alternative music. His sound blends melodic rap, experimental production and contemporary influences, resulting in music that feels fresh, innovative and highly individualistic. Known for his versatility and distinctive artistic identity, he often explores themes of ambition, relationships, self-expression and personal experiences through inventive songwriting. As one of the emerging talents in today's music landscape, Eem Triplin continues to gain attention for his originality, creative vision and rapidly growing influence.

events.description: Founded in 1970, Canadian Brass helped bring the brass quintet to a wide audience with performances that pair polished chamber musicianship with an inviting, conversational spirit. Its expansive repertoire moves from Renaissance and Baroque works to Scott Joplin ragtime, Gershwin, jazz and Broadway, often through inventive arrangements and new commissions. The ensemble’s more than 130 recordings include Stars & Stripes: Canadian Brass Salute America, which reached No. 2 on Billboard’s Classical chart, and Take the “A” Train, a Grammy-nominated album. The appeal lies in hearing five brass players shift effortlessly between musical worlds while making the craft feel lively and close at hand.

events.title: Canadian Brass: Making Spirits Bright
events.venue: George Mason University's Center for the Arts
events.description: Making Spirits Bright “With their unbeatable blend of virtuosity, spontaneity and humor” (The Washington Post), Canadian Brass returns with a delightful program of original arrangements and signature takes on beloved classics, including “It’s the Most Wonderful Time of the Year.” These globetrotting musicians have recorded more than 130 albums and created their own musical world by transcribing, arranging, and commissioning more than 600 works. “Nothing proclaims celebration and festivity like the sound of brass instruments. And if those instruments are played by Canadian Brass, there is even greater cause for celebration” (Toronto Star). This performance is appropriate for all ages. Run Time: approximately 110 minutes, including intermission Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Catch Your Breath
events.description: Catch Your Breath is a rising rock band that has quickly gained attention for its emotionally powerful blend of alternative metal, hard rock, post-hardcore, and melodic modern rock. Formed in Texas, the group has built a passionate fan base through soaring vocal performances, cinematic production, and songs that balance crushing guitar riffs with memorable choruses and deeply personal lyrics. Their music explores themes of resilience, mental health, heartbreak, healing, and self-discovery, creating an authentic connection with listeners who appreciate both emotional vulnerability and hard-hitting musicianship. Catch Your Breath has earned acclaim for energetic live performances that showcase the band's tight chemistry, dynamic stage presence, and ability to recreate the intensity of its studio recordings in concert. As the band continues to expand its catalog and tour alongside some of modern rock's biggest names, Catch Your Breath is establishing itself as one of the most exciting emerging acts in today's heavy music scene.

events.title: Christmas in the Capital: Annapolis Traditions and State House Trees
events.description: Welcome the holidays with Watermark's Christmas in the Capital Tour: Annapolis Traditions and State House Trees. Meet your period-attired guide inside our cozy office before embarking on your tour. Stroll with your colonial guide around Maryland’s capital city, trimmed in greenery for the season. Hear holiday traditions of times past and present as you walk by colonial mansions, Victorian homes, and quaint shops A highlight of the tour is the Maryland State House, with decorated Christmas trees representing the different counties of Maryland, presented by the Federated Garden Clubs of Maryland. The tour ends at Annapolis's grand Christmas tree at Market House Park. Take home the holiday cheer with a goody bag of treats including George Washington’s famed eggnog recipe!

events.title: Christmas Traditions by Candlelight at the William Paca House
events.description: Gather your family and friends and experience the joy of the holiday season with a festive tour of the William Paca House! On this guided candlelit tour, explore holiday traditions that have evolved over time and discover how families in Annapolis and Maryland celebrated the holiday season in generations past. Learn how the Paca household prepared to welcome friends and guests for the holidays. At the conclusion of the tour, enjoy a sweet treat, and a take-home recipe to help bring a taste of the past to your own holiday celebrations. Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in November and December. To see times, visit our November and December event calendar . events.description: Follow your colonial-attired guide through Annapolis’s historic district, highlighting the 18th century, long considered the Golden Age of Annapolis. events.title: Congressional Cemetery Introductory Tour
events.description: Over 67,000 people are interred at Congressional Cemetery, ranging from 1807 all the way until the present day. Their stories are American history in microcosm, all in 35 acres of the nation’s capital. Come and experience their extraordinary lives in a one of kind portal into the past. On this tour of approximately 90 minutes, one of our trained docents will share with you the stories of some of Congressional’s interred residents while walking the beautiful and scenic cemetery grounds. Tickets are only $5 and all proceeds go to benefitting our non-profit mission of historical preservation and education. This is a non-refundable donation. Please come prepared with comfortable and weather-appropriate clothing and shoes, as the tours often stray from the main paths. Tours are rain or shine. Visitors may meet docents at the front gate of the cemetery located at the corner of E St. and Potomac Ave. The cemetery is closed to dogs on Saturdays from 11am – 3pm. Purchase Tickets Here!

Leslye Headland’s “stormy, compassionate, [and] cuttingly observant” ( TimeOut NY ) play interrogates the complexity of family loyalty, the power of religion, and what it truly means to love one another.

events.title: Echoes of Time in Rock Creek Park Guided Hike
events.description: The Milkhouse Ford trail offers both beautifully forested nature and a glimpse into Washington DC’s history. Ramble with a ranger for a guided hike on this 1.7-mile loop, where you will encounter 5000 years of history, from traces of Indigenous land usage, to Fort DeRussy (which saw action during the Civil War), to the two-room log cabin used by poet Joaquin Miller, and to the historic Milkhouse Ford river crossing (one of Rock Creek Park’s oldest and most well-preserved fords). Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing.

events.description: Are you curious about the fascinating history behind Fort Washington? Join us for an enlightening guided tour that delves into the who, what, where, when, and why of this historic fortification! Discover the strategic significance of Digges Point and uncover the reasons it was selected as the ideal site for building the fort. Whether you are a history buff or just looking to enjoy a scenic walk through the fort, this tour is perfect for all ages. Our knowledgeable guides will provide insights into the fort’s construction, its role in defense, and the stories of those who lived and served here. In the event of incliment weather (dangerous heat, thunderstorms, poor air quality, or freezing cold) this program will be moved inside the visitor center and abridge to 30 minutes. Call the Visitor Center at 771-208-1555 or email us prior to your arrival, and we’ll do our best to accommodate your request for a different tour time.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.description: Soar into the spectacle and emotion of Wings , the first film to ever win the Academy Award for Best Picture. Featuring astonishing flight photography and large-scale action sequences that still inspire and awe nearly a century later, Wings combines thrilling adventure with heartfelt human drama. STARS: Clara Bowm Richard Arlen, Charles Rogers, Gary Cooper RUNTIME: 114 Minutes GENRE: Silent, Action, Drama, Romance, War RATING: PG-13 This show is part of the Silent Film Series , celebrating timeless scores and classic films. When the lights go down and the Mighty Wurlitzer rises from the orchestra pit, audiences are treated to a live organ performance featuring Tedde Gibson—complete with a short musical set before the credits roll and a brief introduction to each silent film. Our beloved Wurlitzer turns 100 this December, having filled the theater with music for nearly a century. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop for a unique film experience.

Featuring musicians from Mid-Atlantic favorites Danger Bird, Covered with Jam, Montgomery Warlocks, and the Crimestoppers, GABE delivers an improvisation-driven show built on adventurous jams, musical chemistry, and timeless songs. For more than a decade, GABE has entertained audiences from the Carolinas to New Jersey, with multiple recent sellouts drawing crowds of 200–350+. For venues, GABE offers three passionate fan bases in one compelling show: broader promotional reach, a multigenerational audience, and a proven draw. Live @Hank Dietle's Tavern

events.description: The Manhattans featuring Gerald Alston bring the smooth harmonies and soulful storytelling of a group whose roots stretch back to 1962. Alston joined as lead singer in 1970, fronting the band through a defining run of hits, including the chart-topping ballad “Kiss and Say Goodbye” and the Grammy-winning “Shining Star.” Their catalog also includes “There’s No Me Without You” and “It Feels So Good to Be Loved So Bad,” songs that balance tender vocals with richly arranged R&B. The appeal lies in hearing these enduring melodies carried by the voice that helped make them classics.

events.title: The National Mall Architecture Walking Tour
events.address: Basse of the Washington Monument 2 15th St NW, Washington, DC 20024
events.description: Explore Washington’s most famous monuments and memorials from a fresh perspective. This guided walking tour of the National Mall delves beyond the landmarks to reveal how and why they were constructed. Using architecture and design as our lens, we dive into the powerful stories, historical context, and creative decisions that shaped America’s monumental core. From Pierre L’Enfant’s visionary city plan to bold architectural innovations and contentious design debates, discover the drama and meaning embedded in every stone, statue, and landmark. Whether you’re a first-time visitor or a local who’s walked the Mall a hundred times, this tour will give you a new way to see and understand the heart of the city. Meet your guide at the base of the Washington Monument on the North side (the side facing the White House). The tour takes about 2 hours and covers approximately 1 mile, ending at the Lincoln Memorial. This walking tour is also available for private groups on foot or by car or coach. Visit www.dcdesigntours.com to learn more and sign up.

events.description: Set on Christmas Eve in 1882 Georgetown, The Washington Ballet’s The Nutcracker gives Tchaikovsky’s beloved holiday ballet a distinctly American spin. Choreographed by Septime Webre, this version turns George Washington into Clara’s Nutcracker Prince and reimagines the Rat King as King George III. After a battle with toy soldiers, Clara journeys through an enchanted winter to a springtime of cherry blossoms, where Lady Liberty, John Paul Jones, cardinals and frontier dancers join the celebration. First staged by the company in 1961, this festive blend of classic ballet and playful historical touches makes the familiar tale feel rooted in a particular place and imagination.

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.title: Tuba Christmas
events.description: Christmas…Tuba-style Merry Tubachristmas® will celebrate its 52nd year. Created by Harvey Phillips, Merry Tubachristmas® 2026 concerts will be presented in over 300 cities throughout the United States and in several foreign countries. Tubachristmas® is an annual event created to honor Dr. Harvey G. Phillips’ teacher, mentor, friend, and associate, the late great tubist William J. Bell. Every Tubachristmas® performance features traditional Christmas carols especially arranged by American composer Alec Wilder. Through Wilder, Tubachristmas® concerts pay tribute to composers who have embraced these noble instruments with solo and ensemble compositions. It’s no wonder why the warm toned, smooth organ sounds of the tuba-euphonium choir has won the ears and hearts of every audience, making a Tubachristmas® concert an established Christmas tradition in cities throughout the world Learn more about Tubachristmas® at their official website .

events.address: 301 Watkins Park Drive, Upper Marlboro, MD
events.description: Come support new growers, explore the fields, and take home something delicious at the Urban Farm Incubator at Watkins Regional Park. Every Saturday, 10 am-2 pm , from late May to mid-November , you can shop fresh vegetables, fruit, herbs, and flowers grown on-site by ten emerging farm businesses. events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.description: John Lodge was the legendary bass player, songwriter, and vocalist of Rock & Roll Hall of Fame inductees The Moody Blues. As the songwriter of mega Moody Blues hits including “Ride My See-Saw,” “I’m Just A Singer (In A Rock and Roll Band),” “Isn’t Life Strange,” and more, Lodge performed and recorded with The Moody Blues for more than five decades, selling in excess of 70 million albums worldwide. Following his sad passing in October last year, his son-in-law Jon Davison (of YES), long-term collaborator Alan Hewitt (keyboards for The Moody Blues band), and his daughter Emily came together to create a unique concert to honor John, his life, and the iconic music of The Moody Blues - with the goal to touch hearts, spread happiness, and celebrate what John always described as “the soundtrack of his life.” The premiere in July captured a rare magic by seamlessly weaving archival vocals and footage of John into a live set performed by the musicians who had been by his side for the last ten years. Earning both rave critical reviews and ecstatic fan acclaim, this breathtaking technical feat created an incredibly powerful, spiritual atmosphere where it was as if John were performing in perfect harmony with his band. Attendees described it as having “amazing sound, lights, and live performances,” and calling it “a masterstroke, very emotional & unforgettable.” Continuing in how John's tours honored all of his bandmates, Jon Davison will bring his beautiful, soaring vocals to legendary songs such as "Nights in White Satin" and "Tuesday Afternoon." The show also includes tributes to Ray Thomas and Mike Pinder, together with the stunning video of Graeme Edge reciting "Late Lament" - which he originally recorded for John so that he could always be on stage beside him. John always wanted audiences to leave his shows with joy in their hearts - and that is exactly what this show delivers. All collections must be dropped off at our "Acorn Station" at the Fairfax City Composting Center (10455 Armstrong St) by the end of that Sunday to ensure donation to the Virginia Department of Forestry on Monday, October 12. Each year, the Virginia Department of Forestry collects a variety of species of acorns and nuts that can be planted at its Augusta Nursery to grow into tree seedlings. Certain nuts can be difficult to find regionally, and availability changes year to year. Without the help of volunteers and local seed collection efforts, it's not possible to fill the demand for tree planting projects across the state. That's why the City of Fairfax needs your help to collect seeds this fall. events.title: Cleveland Park & Cathedral Grounds Architecture Tour
events.description: Cleveland Park , dubbed The Queen of the Washington Suburbs in 1903, is one of DC’s most picturesque and architecturally eclectic neighborhoods. The neighborhood, once rolling farmland and a breezy summer escape for Washington’s elite, grew into a thriving streetcar suburb lined with fanciful Queen Anne, stately Colonial Revival, and striking early modernist homes. President Grover Cleveland, who the neighborhood is named for, summered here, and the towering Washington National Cathedral still commands the skyline from its hilltop perch. On this walking tour, we’ll hear about the fascinating history of the second-largest cathedral in the country and explore its charming grounds. We’ll wind through Cleveland Park’s shady streets and uncover how architecture, landscape, and a carefully crafted community identity shaped this neighborhood into one of Washington’s most desirable addresses. Meet your guide outside the main entrance to the Washington National Cathedral, near the glass elevators. This tour-hour tours covers about 1 mile and concludes near the intersection of Wisconsin Avenue and Idaho Avenue NW. Private versions are also available—on foot, by car, or by coach. Visit www.dcdesigntours.com to learn more and reserve your spot.

events.description: Over 67,000 people are interred at Congressional Cemetery, ranging from 1807 all the way until the present day. Their stories are American history in microcosm, all in 35 acres of the nation’s capital. Come and experience their extraordinary lives in a one of kind portal into the past. On this tour of approximately 90 minutes, one of our trained docents will share with you the stories of some of Congressional’s interred residents while walking the beautiful and scenic cemetery grounds. Tickets are only $5 and all proceeds go to benefitting our non-profit mission of historical preservation and education. This is a non-refundable donation. Please come prepared with comfortable and weather-appropriate clothing and shoes, as the tours often stray from the main paths. Tours are rain or shine. Visitors may meet docents at the front gate of the cemetery located at the corner of E St. and Potomac Ave. The cemetery is closed to dogs on Saturdays from 11am – 3pm. Purchase Tickets Here!

Leslye Headland’s “stormy, compassionate, [and] cuttingly observant” ( TimeOut NY ) play interrogates the complexity of family loyalty, the power of religion, and what it truly means to love one another.

Our afternoon begins inside the store, where children can gather for a telling of this beloved holiday tale while enjoying hot chocolate and cookies. Families who register in advance will receive a complimentary nutcracker doll for each child attending, a special keepsake to carry the celebration home. Any remaining nutcrackers will be given away during the event on a first-come, first-served basis, while supplies last . At 4:30 p.m. , we’ll step outside as the Chesapeake Ballet Company brings the story to life beneath the holiday lights. Share in your children’s excitement as they watch the dancers perform. events.title: From Judgment to Compassion
events.description: Join Guest Teacher and US Midwestern National Spiritual Director Gen Kelsang Demo for this Thanksgiving Special Talk. Explore transformative teachings focused on shifting from a mindset of judgment to one of compassion. In this special talk, Gen Keslang Demo, Resident Teacher at the International Kadampa Retreat Center-Grand Canyon and US Midwestern National Spiritual Director, will share practical methods for maintaining a peaceful and compassionate mind, even when faced with challenging people and situations. By learning to distinguish between a person and their delusions, we can begin to let go of judgment and instead develop patience, understanding, and genuine compassion. Through clear explanation and guided reflection, we will explore how all living beings, even those who act negatively, are seeking happiness but are confused about how to find it. Recognizing this allows us to respond with wisdom rather than reactivity, and to protect our own mind from anger and discouragement. By training in these methods, we can learn to keep a positive and balanced mind, contribute to a more harmonious world, and deepen our love for others—without needing to agree with their actions. events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Georgetown Architecture Walking Tour
events.address: 1056 Thomas Jefferson St NW, Washington, DC 20007
events.description: Founded more than 50 years before Washington became the capital, Georgetown began as a gritty port town on the banks of the Potomac. Though it was once dismissed by First Lady Abigail Adams as a “dirty little hole,” today Georgetown is one of DC’s most charming and sought-after neighborhoods. Cobblestone streets lined with colorful rowhouses, elegant churches, and grand mansions tell the story of centuries of change. Our tour explores Georgetown’s evolution from working-class waterfront to wealthy ward, tracing how architecture, commerce, and culture reshaped the neighborhood over centuries. Along the way, we’ll explore hidden alleys, appreciate impressive architectural landmarks, and discuss storied estates. This is Georgetown as you’ve never seen it—perfect for lovers of design, history, and intrigue. Meet your guide at the intersection of Thomas Jefferson Street NW and the C&O Canal. This 2.5 hour walking tour covers about 2.5 miles and ends at Georgetown Waterfront Park near 33rd St and Water Street. Private versions are also available—on foot, by car, or by coach. Visit www.dcdesigntours.com to learn more and reserve your spot.
