events.title: Leanna Firestone
events.description: Leanna Firestone is a Nashville, Tennessee based singer songwriter and multi instrumentalist known for candid, diaristic indie pop. Her songs often draw from uncomfortable memories, awkward moments, and personal experiences, pairing confessional lyrics with acoustic driven production. She began building an audience during the pandemic by sharing original music on TikTok while studying Commercial Songwriting at Middle Tennessee State University. In 2021, her song “Strawberry Mentos” gained traction on the platform, becoming the lead single of her debut EP, Y/N, which has since gained tens of millions of streams across platforms. Firestone has continued to release music steadily, including her album Forward / Slash (2022), the EPs Public Displays of Affection and Good Grief (2023), and fan-favorite single “Becoming Unbecoming” (2024). In 2025, she released her live EP An Evening with Leanna Firestone (Acoustic at The Deli) and toured with Natasha Bedingfield. Her latest album, The Answer, featuring the lead single “Victory Lap, ” was released in May 2026, followed by the first leg of her headline tour across the US and Toronto. With the first half of the tour now complete, Leanna’s second “lap” is set to begin in November 2026. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.description: Discover Frederick’s Past as we Navigate through the Labyrinth of Graves, Crypts and Monuments of Historic Mount Olivet Cemetery. events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Nutcracker Magical Christmas Ballet
events.address: 7750 Capital One Tower Rd, Tysons, VA 22102
events.description: Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet is a dazzling holiday production that reimagines Tchaikovsky's beloved classic with world-class ballet, breathtaking scenery, elaborate costumes, and spectacular theatrical effects. Featuring an international cast of accomplished dancers, the performance combines classical choreography with imaginative storytelling, transporting audiences through Clara's enchanting journey into a magical world filled with toy soldiers, dancing snowflakes, and the unforgettable Kingdom of Sweets. Lavish sets, larger-than-life puppetry, soaring acrobatics, and innovative stage illusions enhance the timeless score, creating a visually stunning experience that appeals to both longtime ballet enthusiasts and first-time theatergoers. While honoring the traditions that have made The Nutcracker a cherished holiday favorite for generations, the production introduces fresh artistic elements that add excitement and wonder to every performance. With its blend of exceptional dance, memorable music, and festive holiday magic, Nutcracker! Magical Christmas Ballet has become an annual tradition for families seeking an unforgettable seasonal celebration.

events.description: State Champs is a pop-punk band celebrated for its infectious energy, hook-filled songwriting, and high-octane live performances that have made it a leading force in modern rock. Formed in Albany, New York, the group quickly gained recognition with acclaimed albums such as The Finer Things, Around the World and Back, Living Proof, and Kings of the New Age, blending punchy guitar riffs, soaring choruses, and emotionally resonant lyrics into a signature sound. Fronted by vocalist Derek DiScanio, State Champs crafts songs that explore friendship, relationships, personal growth, and perseverance while maintaining the upbeat spirit that defines the genre. Their concerts are renowned for nonstop audience participation, energetic sing-alongs, and an undeniable chemistry that transforms every performance into a celebration of pop-punk culture. Through relentless touring, consistently strong releases, and an unwavering commitment to authentic songwriting, State Champs has earned its place among the most respected and influential bands in today's pop-punk scene.

Their 2021 EP, Prologue... Tracks such as “clean.” and “such.a.shame” capture the push between abrasion and melody, while “Lye solution” brings in collaborators from Loathe, BVDLVD and Hail the Sun. The result gives their music both a cathartic punch and a vivid sense of narrative.

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.title: Wreath Making Crafternoon
events.description: Step back into a time when holiday décor was gathered from the woods and the winter garden. Join us for an immersive workshop dedicated to the art of the traditional, textured wreath. Moving away from the commercial look of the modern holiday, we will focus on the rich diversity of “The Winter Field”—utilizing layered evergreens, architectural dried elements, and the “saved” treasures of late autumn. What You’ll Explore: The Power of Texture: Learn to layer multiple varieties of cedar, pine, and fir for a lush, professional-grade base. The Dried Garden: Integrating natural elements like seed pods, dried citrus, red chilis and flowers for a modern take on the “Nature-First” aesthetic. Organic Mechanics: Mastering the traditional wire-wrap technique to ensure your wreath stays fresh and secure through the season.

events.title: Les Misérables-Olney Theatre
events.description: Modern classics don’t come any bigger than Les Misérables, and Olney Theatre celebrates it for the first time in honor of the show’s 40th anniversary. Based on Victor Hugo’s sweeping 19th-century novel of redemption, revolution, and love, the songs of Les Miz conquered Broadway in the 1980s and continue to resonate in this third decade of the 21st Century. Follow Jean-Valjean from his beginnings as convict #24601 to life in hiding, to protector of Cosette, pursued all the while by the relentless Javert, culminating in the revolutionary passions of the 1832 Paris uprising. Join us at the barricade this holiday season, and be stirred by a musical unmatched by its lyrical humor, its calls for justice, and its portrayal of the sacrifices one can make in the name of love. Featuring: Kevin S. McAllister as Javert, Alex De Bard as Eponine, Tracy Lynn Olivera as Madame Thénardier, Jordan Friend as Thénardier, Stephanie Waters as Fantine, Ben Clark as Marius, and more to be announced soon.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.description: Yuki Chiba, formerly known as KOHH, is a Tokyo rapper whose direct, unhurried delivery and inventive beats have made him a distinctive voice in Japanese hip-hop. He returned under his own name with the 2024 single “Team Tomodachi,” then released the album STAR; international listeners also know him from his feature on Megan Thee Stallion’s “Mamushi.” His catalog moves between punchy rap and more atmospheric sounds, including the collaborative album separated at birth with producer Stillz. That range gives his music an engaging contrast: sharp, catchy tracks alongside more spacious, reflective textures.

events.title: Yuki Chiba - First North America Headline Tour
events.description: With lyrics that read like a personal diary, an inimitable flow, and an ability to jump across genres, Yuki Chiba’s music has a raw honesty and natural flawlessness that continues to inspire fans worldwide. His first song under the name Yuki Chiba was “Team Tomodachi” (Released February 2024), which became a viral sensation. In June 2024, his collaboration with Megan Thee Stallion, “Mamushi, ” exploded. The song went #1 on the Rhythmic Airplay Chart and Yuki’s performance of it at the VMAs made him the first Japanese artist to grace the Music Video Award’s stage. From then, within the span of about 6 months, Chiba released a staggering 3 albums; “STAR” , “Okumanchoja” (Millionaire), and “Eien” (Eternity), as well as a collaboration with creative maven, Stillz, entitled “separated at birth. ” In July 2025, Yuki sold-out the Budokan Arena in Tokyo for a triumphant hometown show. He was Japanese Rolling Stone’s August 2025 cover star. Furthermore, he penned the official anthem for the popular Riot Games’ franchise VALORANT, and continues to release collaborative music with artists such as Murda Beatz, Feid, and Big Sean. In 2026, Yuki has made his headline touring debuts in Australia

events.title: CCAS Academy: The Hidden Life of Plastics: What’s Really in Our Water? featuring Lauren Pincus (Zoom)
events.description: CCAS Academy: The Hidden Life of Plastics: What’s Really in Our Water? featuring Lauren Pincus (Zoom)LocationZoom Event DescriptionWhat happens to plastic after it enters our environment? Join Lauren Pincus for an exploration of microplastics and their growing presence in our waterways. Drawing on current scientific research‚ Lauren will examine how microplastics enter aquatic environments‚ interact with environmental contaminants‚ and what scientists are learning about their potential long-term effects on ecosystems and human health. Through an introduction to her laboratory’s research and an inside look at some of its fascinating findings‚ attendees will learn how scientists collect‚ process‚ and analyze environmental samples to better understand the presence and impact of microplastics. Lauren will also demonstrate how researchers investigate these tiny particles and uncover what they reveal about the health of our waterways. More about Assistant Professor Lauren Pincus Dr. Pincus’ research aims to examine complexation of inorganic pollutants by natural and engineered solids using advanced synchrotron spectroscopy techniques in order to understand and control the fate and transport of inorganic pollutants in the environment‚ develop novel sustainable and selective materials for aqueous contaminant removal‚ and design new technologies for climate change mitigation.

events.title: Cherish the Ladies: Celtic Christmas
events.description: For four decades, Cherish the Ladies has been a leading ensemble in Irish traditional music, known for performances that combine instrumental virtuosity, vocals, and step dance. Led by Joanie Madden—a flute and whistle player and National Endowment for the Arts National Heritage Fellow—the Grammy-nominated group has released 18 albums, toured internationally, and collaborated with symphony orchestras. This holiday season, the ensemble presents its Celtic Christmas program, featuring arrangements of traditional carols including “Angels We Have Heard on High,” “The First Noel,” and “Silent Night.” Drawing on a repertoire developed across several holiday recordings— On Christmas Night, A Star in the East, and Christmas in Ireland —the performance highlights Celtic instrumentation, vocal harmonies, and step dancing, with guest vocalists and dancers joining throughout. The concert features Madden alongside Mirella Murray (accordion), Nollaig Casey (fiddle), Hannah Collins (piano), Mary Coogan (guitar), and Cheryl Prashker (percussion), joined by vocalists and guitarists Kate Purcell, Don Stiffe, and Bruce Foley. She has worn many hats as a businesswoman, mother, wife, widow, TV personality, author, radio host, and DJ. But of all the things she’s accomplished, her greatest feat is becoming confident in learning how to do things completely on her own. Fear is practically baked into our culture—especially for women. But we can choose another way to live, using confidence to move forward and fear as a tool of encouragement to pivot when life’s challenges knock us down. In this film, some of the world's most talented filmmakers give us a behind-the-scenes look at what it takes to bring these powerful visual stories to life, and how they stay inspired and passionate for their next project. Included with museum admission.

events.title: Giving Back on GivingTuesday! Join Us for a Healthy Forests Day of Action
events.description: This GivingTuesday, roll up your sleeves and help keep our local forests healthy! Scenic Rivers is teaming up with the Chesapeake Bay Foundation and Save our Trees (a program of Anne Arundel County Watershed Stewards Academy) for a special Healthy Forests volunteer workday removing invasive English ivy from trees at the Philip Merrill Environmental Center in Annapolis. The Chesapeake Bay Foundation’s beautiful waterfront campus is protected by a Scenic Rivers & MET conservation easement, and we’re excited to work together to care for this special place! Our GivingTuesday volunteers braved cold, rainy weather last year and still got an incredible amount of work done. We’re hoping for a little more sunshine this year, and we’ll celebrate a job well done with pizza on the deck overlooking the Bay! As part of Scenic Rivers Healthy Forests program, volunteers will work in designated areas of the conservation easement to remove English ivy from trees. Invasive vines can damage and weaken trees. Removing harmful invasive vines is an important step toward protecting the health of our local forests. No experience necessary! We’ll provide training on how to identify and safely remove English ivy. Scenic Rivers and Save Our Trees will provide work gloves and tools, though volunteers are welcome to bring their own. What to Wear and Bring: Wear long sleeves, long pants, and closed-toe shoes. Poison ivy is present in the work areas. Bring a full water bottle. Dress for the weather! We’ll be working outdoors in early December. Keeping our forests healthy takes teamwork! GivingTuesday is the perfect opportunity to make a difference right here in our community. We hope you’ll join us! Questions? Contact Scenic Rivers Stewardship and Engagement Coordinator, Luke Lanham, at Luke@srlt.org or 443.714.7756.

events.title: Kate Voegele "Then & Now" Tour
events.description: Singer-songwriter and One Tree Hill alum Kate Voegele returns to the stage with Then & Now, an intimate new tour built around the songs — and the stories behind them. After revisiting the music of One Tree Hill on tour last year, Voegele is digging deeper into the catalog this time, bringing back songs from her years as Mia Catalano that haven’t been heard live in years alongside music from her new album, Age of Alchemy. Built around storytelling and songwriting, Then & Now traces the unexpected threads between songs Voegele wrote at the beginning of her career and the artist she is today — how the same emotions change with time, what she understands differently now, and the stories behind the songs that she’s never shared before. Part concert, part trip through the pages of her songwriting history, Then & Now offers fans a rare chance to experience nearly two decades of Kate Voegele’s music in a completely new way: the old songs, the new songs, and everything that happened in between. events.title: What Do We Mean By PrEP (Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis)?
events.description: What Do We Mean By PrEP? Featuring Dr. Maranda Ward, '17, Associate Professor and Director of Equity, Department of Clinical Research & Leadership, GW School of Medicine and Health Sciences PrEP, or Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis, is a safe and highly effective medication that helps prevent HIV infection. Yet many people and communities who could benefit from PrEP are not using it. Why? In this talk, Dr. Maranda Ward will explore how public health messaging, research, and healthcare practices shape people's understanding of PrEP and influence who feels seen, supported, and informed when making decisions about HIV prevention. Drawing on her research, Dr. Ward will discuss the importance of moving beyond stigma and deficit-based narratives toward approaches that recognize the strengths, experiences, and realities of diverse communities. The talk will explore PrEP's role in HIV prevention, the structural inequities that continue to affect access and uptake, and why equitable, intersectional communication and education is essential to reaching and resonating with those who stand to benefit most. events.description: What Do We Mean By PrEP? Featuring Dr. Maranda Ward, '17, Associate Professor and Director of Equity, Department of Clinical Research & Leadership, GW School of Medicine and Health Sciences PrEP, or Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis, is a safe and highly effective medication that helps prevent HIV infection. Yet many people and communities who could benefit from PrEP are not using it. Why? In this talk, Dr. Maranda Ward will explore how public health messaging, research, and healthcare practices shape people's understanding of PrEP and influence who feels seen, supported, and informed when making decisions about HIV prevention. Drawing on her research, Dr. Ward will discuss the importance of moving beyond stigma and deficit-based narratives toward approaches that recognize the strengths, experiences, and realities of diverse communities. The talk will explore PrEP's role in HIV prevention, the structural inequities that continue to affect access and uptake, and why equitable, intersectional communication and education is essential to reaching and resonating with those who stand to benefit most. About Dr. Maranda Ward: Dr. Maranda C. Ward is an Associate Professor in the Department of Clinic

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: The Milkhouse Ford trail offers both beautifully forested nature and a glimpse into Washington DC’s history. Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing.

events.description: The Blackbyrds performing this special concert on Thanksgiving weekend to celebrate 50 years since the release of “Rock Creek Park”, a classic song that has endured for generations! The band is one of the most successful ever from the DC area and came together in the 1970s as Howard University students under the guidance of their music professor, the late great jazz trumpeter Donald Byrd who became their manager and producer. They created a unique jazz funk sound combined with soulful harmonies that made a big impact on the music charts. The Blackbyrds’ biggest hit songs were “Walking In Rhythm”, their Grammy nominated million selling smash hit on both the R&B and pop charts; “Happy Music”, an uplifting party anthem that was their biggest R&B hit; and “Rock Creek Park”, their beloved song known for its infectious groove and famous verse “doin’ it in the park, doin’ it after dark, oh yeah…Rock Creek Park!” The Blackbyrds tour around the world but always look forward to performing in the DC area where they are most appreciated. The band’s original core members as well as new members are all from the DC area led by drummer Keith Killgo. Their crowd pleasing performance features all of their most popular songs plus those by Donald Byrd including “Places And Spaces” and “(Fallin’ Like) Dominoes.” SATURDAY, NOV 28. 2026 Dinner & Doors 6:00pm Showtime 8:00pm

events.description: We invite you to join National Park Service volunteer and expert birder Molly Hermann for an engaging bird walk at Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens. This event is open to all, including those new to birding. We encourage participants to bring water, sunscreen, and binoculars if available. A limited number of binoculars are available for loan with a photo ID. The walk will be conducted at a leisurely pace, covering approximately one mile. We will gather in front of the visitor center, and the duration of the walk will typically range from 1.5 to 2 hours, depending on our observations. We look forward to sharing this delightful experience with you!
